numeric_arrays.binary64: real64[] - runtime-sized array of `real64` (IEEE-754 binary64), created with array(nat(n), fill = 0.0) and indexed with [i]
numeric_arrays.integer64: int[] - runtime-sized array of exact arbitrary-precision `int`, created with array(nat(n), fill = 0); the fixed-width arithmetic kernel MB-03 uses `int64`
numeric_arrays.allocation: value semantics; arrays are contiguous native storage with bounds and initialization checks; workload arrays are passed to helpers by reference (`int[] &`) so no copy is made except where the workload itself copies (MB-07's per-round copy is an ordinary value assignment)

string_buffer.buffer: nat8[] - the mutable byte buffer used by MB-08 passes 1-4; obtained once before the timed region from the joined text with nat8[](text.utf8())
string_buffer.string: string - immutable UTF-8 text; built fresh inside each MB-08 round from the buffer with string.from_utf8(bin(buffer))
string_buffer.string_access: string.codepoints() - the string type's own scalar-sequence accessor, iterated in order for MB-08 pass 5
string_buffer.direct_character_access: yes: text[index] returns a one-code-point string and .codepoints() returns the scalar sequence

file_io.writer: file.write writer(path) creates a file.write stream; .writer(text) writes each line and the stream closes at the end of the write_round function
file_io.reader: file.read reader(path) creates a file.read stream; while .reader(string &line) yields one line (bool | error) until EOF
file_io.incremental: true - the file.write and file.read operators perform incremental I/O; the runtime buffering is not configurable, so the frozen 65536-byte buffer size cannot be requested and language-provided buffering is measured (per micro.md section 4.12(c))

collections.map: map<int, int> - the standard insertion-ordered open-addressing map; empty bare declaration, get(k) -> int | none, set, has, remove, keys(), values()
collections.set: distinct<int> - the standard insertion-ordered unique-value collection; a bare declaration creates an empty collection
collections.allocator: the language's ordinary managed value storage; no allocator choice exists

monotonic_clock.api: time.now() -> time.Instant and time.since(start) -> time.Duration; elapsed nanoseconds are math.round(duration.seconds() * 1000000000.0)

runtime_checks.effective_behavior: always on under the frozen recipe `quidra build FILE.qui -o BIN`: fixed-width integer overflow, negative nat results, division by zero, array bounds, uninitialized reads, numeric cast range and the call-depth guard terminate deterministically with status 101; native code is otherwise optimized with Clang -O3 without fast-math
